slides.title:
More people, but
much more money.
slides.body:
Seoul counted 11.56 million foreign visitors from January to August 2026, a record, up 21.6% from 9.51 million. Their card spending rose far faster: 7.78 trillion won against 4.87 trillion a year earlier, up 59.9%.

That is roughly 2.8 times the growth rate of visitor numbers, and in eight months it already reached about 98% of the 7.94 trillion won spent across all of 2025. August alone brought 1.72 million visitors and 1.03 trillion won — the fifth straight month above a trillion. Seoul now takes 71.1% of all foreign offline card spending in Korea.

slides.by: Percentage growth off a small base is the easiest number to misread. Lotte Members' analysis of Korea Tourism Organization card data for May 2026 put Myeong-dong at 27.8% of all foreign spending nationwide, against 5.7% for Seongsu-dong and 3.2% for Yeouido-dong. Seongsu is growing roughly twice as fast and remains about a fifth of Myeong-dong's size. This post is research, not a personal visit — every figure comes from a published source, checked on 10 October 2026.

caption:
Seoul published its foreign-spending numbers this week, and the gap between the two headline figures is the whole story. Visitors from January to August 2026: 11.56 million, a record, up 21.6%. Their card spending: 7.78 trillion won, up 59.9% — about 2.8 times the growth rate of the visitor count, and already around 98% of everything spent in all of 2025.

The more useful number is where it went. Foreign card spending in Seoul's back-alley commercial districts rose 80.9%, the highest growth of any district type in the city. Near Dosan Park it rose 240.1%. In the Gyeongsu School pocket of Seongsu-dong, 206.6%. At Gwangjang Market, 127.4%. Seongsu overall came in at 103.7% and its cafe street at 109.3%. Myeong-dong, at 74.7%, was the slowest of the group.

Two things worth holding onto before you redraw your map. First, most of this is not food: shopping took 46.6% of the total and medical and wellness 23.8%, leaving food and drink at 13.2% — though dining spend did rise 59.5%. Second, a growth rate is not a size. Lotte Members put Myeong-dong at 27.8% of nationwide foreign spending in May against Seongsu's 5.7%. Seongsu is growing about twice as fast and is still roughly a fifth as big.

So the practical read is not 'skip Myeong-dong'. It is that the quiet residential block you were planning to discover has already been discovered, and a weekday morning is now the difference between a street and a queue. Sources in the last slide.
